evidence.source: 漢字構形資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: 字形演變; oracle-bone and bronze form records
evidence.text: The record identifies the oracle-bone example as 合集19050 and the bronze example as 集成02836. Its editorial analysis says 天 and 元 refer to the head, and describes 天 as a frontal standing person whose emphasized head mark was later simplified to a horizontal stroke; it proposes extension from head to the sky above. These are the database’s paleographic interpretation and source identifiers, not independently dated readings of each artifact.
evidence.title: 漢字「天」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry analyzes the graph as a standing person with an emphasized head and reports head-related use in oracle-bone inscription 合集20975, personal-name use, and 天邑商 (also called 大邑商). It reports bronze uses for 天帝, 天命, and 天子, and Warring States bamboo-slip uses of 天命 and 天下. The page gives corpus identifiers but not absolute dates for each cited token, and it does not establish an unbroken semantic path between the senses.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：天

evidence.source: 陳家寧, 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.field: section II, 天與大是同源字, paragraphs 114–129
evidence.text: The author surveys oracle-bone and bronze forms as 大-like human figures with the head marked, and cites examples 天邑商 in 合集36535/36542 alongside 大邑商 in 合集36482/36530 and on the He zun. The article argues that 天 and 大 were interchangeable or closely related in Shang-Zhou usage, while discussing uncertainty about their exact graphic and lexical relationship. These examples caution against treating every early 天 occurrence as unambiguously ‘sky/heaven’; they do not prove that the spoken word 天 originated with the sense ‘great’.
evidence.title: 陳家寧：說“大”、“太”和“天”的關係

evidence.source: 許慎, 說文解字, online text and 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.text: The entry reads 顚也。至高無上，从一、大. Duan Yucai explains 顚 as the top of a person and treats 天 as a general designation for what is highest. This is a historical lexicographic analysis; it is not independent proof of the earliest spoken sense.
evidence.title: 說文解字「天」

evidence.text: The inspected file description identifies 天-oracle.svg as a vector redraw of 天 in Shang oracle-script style, cites a specific Xiaoxuetang glyph image as its source, and records CC0 1.0. The selected illustration is a modern digital redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact.
evidence.title: File:天-oracle.svg

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Academia Sinica form record, CUHK inscription analysis, Fudan specialist discussion, Shuowen entry, and exact Commons file description. The Unicode character-specific record could not be opened. The Commons original-file link was identified on its inspected description page, but direct opening failed.

gaps: The inspected sources do not independently establish absolute dates for each cited oracle-bone or bronze token; artifact identifiers and script labels are available, but no precise dated sequence was verified here.

The earliest attested graph and earliest spoken sense remain distinct questions. Head-related oracle-bone usage is reported by CUHK and Academia Sinica, while sky-first analysis appears in the dossier’s tertiary source; available evidence does not establish a single certain semantic chronology or a complete head/top-to-sky chain.
The Fudan discussion supports interchange between 天 and 大 in Shang-Zhou usage but does not by itself show that 天’s spoken word originated with a ‘great’ meaning.
No inspected source reports graphic corruption. The documented mark-to-horizontal-stroke change is described as simplification.
No phonetic component is proposed: 一 and 大 are discussed as graphic elements in historical analyses, and no sound-component role is supported here.

The local Baxter–Sagart row provided for 天 is *l̥ˤi[n], with MC then and a western-dialect MC xen entry under the same OC notation; no component row applies. The official upstream PDF was not rechecked in this invocation, so the local dataset is not external evidence.
The official Unicode GetUnihanData record for U+5929 failed to open. The dossier-provided local Unihan row kMandarin=tiān is not represented here as externally verified evidence.

The Commons original SVG link was visible on the inspected file description page, but opening that direct link failed in the web tool. The page itself records CC0 and the Xiaoxuetang provenance; the glyph has not been visually inspected in this research.

items.period: Shang-style oracle script (modern redraw of an ancient form; exact exemplar identified on Commons as Xiaoxuetang image 41.E045)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of a Shang-style oracle-bone form of 天, showing the early graph discussed as a person with an emphasized head.
items.alt: Black oracle-script glyph for 天, redrawn as a vector.
items.selection_reason: The exact Commons description identifies the character, its script style, specific Xiaoxuetang source image, and reuse rights. It illustrates the head-mark interpretation while remaining clearly identified as a modern redraw.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 as stated on the Commons description page; the page also attributes the source glyph image to Xiaoxuetang.

limitations.text: The Commons original-file link was established from the inspected description page, but its direct URL could not be opened during this research; no visual inspection of image pixels is claimed.
The cited ancient-form identifications and graphic analysis are source descriptions and editorial interpretations; precise dates for each individual inscription token were not verified.
